author: Yellowpantstime
title: A Printing App That Makes Its Own Print Menu Unreadable
content:
This app is astonishingly bad at the one thing it is supposed to do: print.

On an iPhone in Dark Mode, the print-options menu can display white text on a white background, making the controls completely unreadable. That is not a minor cosmetic glitch. It makes the app functionally unusable. The official workaround is apparently to change the appearance setting for the entire phone just to use HP’s app, which is absurd.

HP has had ample time and resources to fix a basic interface defect that should never have passed quality control in the first place. Instead, customers who already paid for HP hardware are left troubleshooting an app that cannot reliably display its own menus.

A printer app should make printing easier. This one adds frustration, wastes time, and reflects an embarrassing lack of attention to basic usability.

title: There isn’t really a point to it…
content: The HP Printing App feels like it exists mostly to stand in the doorway and remind you that your printer would love to become a subscription service. I downloaded it because I needed one very normal, very useful feature: the ability to adjust an image’s print size. Somehow, amid all the promotional nudges and extra menus, that option is nowhere to be found. Instead, the app adds another layer between me and a task that should take ten seconds. The printer itself gives me just as much useful information, and at least it does not keep trying to sell me on a monthly relationship. It works, technically, but it adds more bloat than value. Two stars for existing and connecting. The rest is mostly vibes, subscriptions, and missed opportunities.

author: Insta-ink sucks
title: Overcharging
content:
The printer works great. Really enjoy the app. My complaint is that I should not have to pay HP for every page I print. That’s ridiculous, and it gets expensive. It’s just another way for HP (and other like-companies) to suck the common person dry while raking in the billions. It was never like this growing up. I bought the printer, paper, and ink, and printed my hearts desire until the paper or ink ran out. 

And I realize that’s still an option, but the ink cartridges you sell in the store are expensive and only last about 50 pages and they’re done! You basically give me no choice but to sign up for your insta-ink BS because in the long run it actually ends up being a little cheaper than buying the cartridges, which isn’t saying much. 

All I want HP to do is sell me a printer and ink and then I’ll go my merry way. I don’t want to be hooked on your insta-ink dependency chain.
